text:
alex k: Morning handoff — quick summary of overnight and what to watch for. paging happened 03:14UTC for high p95 on streaming endpoints, triggered ~60 pages (primarily dedicated pools). Incident bot logged alert: INCIDENT-9876.

oncall-bot: Pager summary: 60 pages, escalations: 2, auto-suppressed: 18, customers affected: ~4 (partial degradation).

Maya S: TL;DR — root cause seems to be Dedicated autoscaler thrash: multiple nodes were added/removed in 5m windows causing KV cache churn and route flaps. Streaming tail p99 spiked (1.6s -> 3.8s) and some streaming sessions aborted.

Li Chen: Confirmed from telemetry: autoscaler oscillation was triggered by a bug in the burst policy where short-lived cpu spikes from a quantized model warmup were treated as sustained load. We saw rollout of a new burst-policy config at 02:48UTC (canary) that hit production pools.

Samir: Customer impact notes: 3 customers reported partial failures for streaming completions (session resets). No data loss. SLO degradation for those routes ~20m window. Support already opened tickets with customers A and B (non-blocking).

alex k: Immediate mitigation taken overnight: reverted canary config (02:56UTC), temporarily disabled burst-autoscale for affected dedicated pool, and enabled routing fallback to smaller-quant model (redwood-quant-v2) for streaming routes. That restored session stability but tail p99 still slightly elevated (~2.1s).

incident-bot: INCIDENT-9876 status changed: INVESTIGATING -> MONITORING (03:40UTC). Postmortem channel: #incidents/postmortems-9876.

Maya S: Current status: primary cluster stable, one pool still shows 10% elevated evictions — probably leftover KV rewarm. We're running a KV cache backfill job which should finish in ~30-45m.

Li Chen: Ops notes / runbook snippets I used:
````
- Runbook: Dedicated autoscaler thrash 
  https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dedicated-autoscaler-thrash
- Temporary fix: disable-burst-autoscale.sh --pool <pool-id>
- Fallback route: routing-policies -> prefer redwood-quant-v2 for streaming-heavy routes
````

Samir: Action items for current shift:
- primary: Maya S (you remain primary until 12:00 UTC)
- secondary: Alex K (on-call for escalation)
- coverage gap: 03:00-04:00 UTC had partial overlap; make sure to call out if you need SRE help for cluster ops

Maya S: I'm going to keep an eye on the backfill progress and watch for any blackhole routing errors. If eviction rate doesn't fall below 2% by 04:30UTC we should re-run cache warmup with a slower concurrency (see runbook).

alex k: Notes for next shift (put in the handoff ticket):
- If thrash recurs: pin autoscaler to stable config (use tag: autoscaler-2026-01-stable) and hold canary rollout.
- If KV backfill fails: escalate to eng-runtime and run manual restore from snapshot (`kv-restore --snapshot-id <id>`).
- Customer comms: support to send an update by EOD to impacted customers; engineering to provide timeline if backfill >1h.

Samir: Post-handoff checklist (Maya -> next primary):
- check incident-bot for any new pages matching INCIDENT-9876 or similar memory/eviction alerts
- verify routing fallback remains active for streaming routes (route-table id: rt-stream-23)
- ensure autoscaler canary is blocked until we confirm the fix in the burst-policy logic PR (PR #8345).

Maya S: Added runbook links to the handoff ticket: https://redwood.internal/handoff/2372004321. I'm leaving a short playbook in the ticket for the next oncall.

alex k: Anything else? otherwise I'll mark this handoff thread as the official morning summary. :thumbsup:

Li Chen: One more: postmortem owners — Li Chen + Samir. Timing: draft by EOD today, final after blameless review next week.

Maya S: Acknowledged. I'm staying on as primary for the next 2.5 hours and will escalate if we see reflare.

alex k: Thanks team.
